## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

It recounts the bodhisatta's practice of perfection (*cariyā*) while reborn as the nāga king Campeyya. In comparative scholarship on canonical Pali narrative literature, André Bareau identifies it as the thirteenth story of the *Cariyāpiṭaka* in relation to the broader Jātaka tradition [Bareau].

In machine-computed textual analysis by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits Pali-internal text reuse with the post-canonical commentary tradition, specifically sharing two passages (666 characters in total) with the first part of Buddhaghosa's *Visuddhimagga* (*Visuddhimaggo: Paṭhamo bhāgo*), where verses §2.2–5.4 align closely with §1838–1845 (similarity score 0.88) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels meeting the significance threshold (score ≥ 10) are recorded by DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
